draft.title: Theories of change
card: A theory of change is a way of explaining why societies change. Two common theories give different answers.
sees society as a system of parts that work together, like organs in a body. Change happens when society adjusts so that it stays stable and keeps working.
sees society as made up of groups with different amounts of power and resources. Change is the result of struggles between these groups, as less powerful groups push against those who hold power.
Both theories can be used on the same change. A functionalist asks how it helps society keep working. A conflict theorist asks which groups gained or lost power.
draft.remember: Functionalism explains change as adjustment for stability. Conflict theory explains it as struggle for power.

a.q: Which statement about a change in society is made from a conflict theory view?
opts: Workers pushed employers for power through strikes
Schools adapted so society could keep running smoothly
Laws were updated so that society kept its stability
Each part of society changed to support the others
a.why: Conflict theory sees change as coming from a struggle between groups, such as workers and employers, over power. The other options describe parts of society adjusting to keep it stable, which is the functionalist view.
a.clue: Look for the option with groups in a struggle.

b.q: A town's council changes bus routes after many residents move to a new suburb. It says the change keeps the town running well for everyone. Which theory does this explanation fit, and why?
opts: Functionalism, because it shows the town adjusting to stay stable
Functionalism, because it shows groups struggling for power
Conflict theory, because it shows the town adjusting for stability
Conflict theory, because it shows a change affecting people
b.why: The council describes a change that helps the town keep working, which is society adjusting to stay stable. That is the functionalist view. Conflict theory would ask which groups gained or lost power, and the explanation does not do this.
b.clue: Does the explanation talk about stability or about power?
